content:
SELECTED_INDEX: 2
CONFIDENCE: 0.31
EXPLANATION: The very strong Raman band at 2104 cm⁻¹ together with the sharp band at 3292 cm⁻¹ is characteristic of a terminal C≡C group (ν(C≡C) ≈ 2100 cm⁻¹ and ν(C≡C–H) ≈ 3300 cm⁻¹).  
Several candidates contain a terminal alkyne, but the spectrum also shows a cluster of medium–strong bands at 1036, 1066 and 1079 cm⁻¹ plus a band at 1167 cm⁻¹. These lie in the typical ether C–O–C and C–O stretching region (≈ 1000–1150 cm⁻¹), while no broad O–H stretch (≈ 3200–3600 cm⁻¹, broad) is present, indicating ether oxygens rather than alcohol O–H. Among the candidates, only molecule 2 (C#CCCOC1COC1) possesses a terminal alkyne together with two C–O–C ether linkages, providing the required vibrational features.  
Aliphatic C–H stretches at 2870–2950 cm⁻¹ and CH₂ scissoring at 1445 cm⁻¹ match the long aliphatic chain in 2, and the 678/632 cm⁻¹ pair fits acetylenic C–H bending modes. Compounds lacking an alkyne (5) or containing a nitrile (10) are inconsistent with the 2104 cm⁻¹ position, while purely hydrocarbon diacetylenes (1) would be expected to show an additional strong internal C≡C Raman band near 2200 cm⁻¹ that is absent here. Hence candidate 2 best explains the observed peak pattern.
